articles.title: Experience: I helped jail the teacher who groomed me
articles.summary: At 15, having the cool 31-year-old PE teacher single me out felt thrilling. It took years to see his praise for what it really was. I was 15 when Paul joined my high school in Queensland, Australia, as a PE teacher. He was fun and handsome, and seemed much younger than his 31 years.
body: He’d always stop for a chat. I was the only child of a single mum and though she was there for me, I didn’t confide in her. But he was easy to talk to and I quickly developed a crush.
“You’ve got a muscly bum,” he remarked one day. “I can see it through your shorts.”
I began to wonder if he liked me back. During athletics training he would deliberately step into my path so that I’d collide with him.
Other people were starting to notice Paul’s interest. I denied we were getting close, but rumours kept swirling and he was eventually suspended.
points: At 15, having the cool 31-year-old PE teacher single me out felt thrilling.
It took years to see his praise for what it really was.

articles.title: Benjamina Ebuehi’s recipe for steamed chocolate puddings with malted chocolate sauce | The sweet spot
articles.summary: It’s steamed pudding season again, and there are few better ways to serve it than with hot chocolate sauce and a scoop of ice-cream. This is the best time of the year for proper stodge, and an even better time to make steamed puddings.
body: Grease seven small pudding basins (of about 170-190ml capacity) with butter and cut out a small round of baking paper to fit in the bases.

Put the butter and sugar in a bowl and beat for two to three minutes, until smooth and creamy. Whisk in the eggs one at a time, then sift in the flour, cocoa powder, baking powder and salt, stirring just until the mix comes together and there are no pockets of flour hiding in the bottom of the bowl. Stir in the milk, then divide the batter evenly between the greased and lined basins.

Put seven small sheets of foil on top of seven pieces of baking paper, make a pleat in the middle of each, then put them paper side down on top of each pudding basin. Scrunch the edges to hold the lids in place.

Put a wide pan on the hob and put a steaming tray or upturned plate inside. Add the pudding basins and fill with enough hot water to come about halfway up the sides of the puddings. Cover and leave to steam for 40-45 minutes, until the puddings feel firm to the touch. Unwrap and turn out on to plates.
points: It’s steamed pudding season again, and there are few better ways to serve it than with hot chocolate sauce and a scoop of ice-cream.

articles.title: This Fashion Scion’s Laid-Back Ibiza Wedding Featured Lace Dresses, Barefoot Vows, and Dancing Till Dawn
articles.summary: Lola Teller walked down the aisle flanked by her parents, fashion photographer and stylist Venetia Scott and photographer Juergen Teller, to marry Freddie Woodruff in an Ibizan pine grove.
body: There were even more visits—10 in total—to Kensington-based bridal designer Phillipa Lepley to perfect the lace wedding dress, complete with corset, veil, and train, and designed with the input of her mom. Having a mother behind some of Vogue ’s most memorable covers must have come in handy? “Throughout the process, she was making me try on these enormous poofs of dresses, which looked great but were never gonna be the one for me,” Lola says. “Often I’d be like, ‘I like this!’, and then mum would be like, ‘...No.’ She’s always right, though.”

On the day, she paired the dress with white silk platform heels from “not a nice brand,” and diamond-and-pearl drop earrings borrowed from her stepmother’s collection. She would walk down the aisle flanked by her mom and dad, Juergen Teller, though despite having two of fashion’s most directional photographers at her fingertips, she still hired traditional wedding photographers to document the occasion. “Well, you want some of the classic shots,” she explains. “Plus, they wanted to enjoy themselves.” Indeed, Lola says Teller didn’t take “a single photo” throughout the weekend.

articles.title: What the “Ferritin Face” Trend Says About the Future of Beauty
articles.summary: First came “cortisol face”, then “Ozempic face”. Now, TikTok is diagnosing low iron through dark circles and thinning hair, cultivating the latest viral trend du jour.
body: Dark circles? A dull, washed-out complexion? Hair that’s seemingly shedding more than usual, or nails that break at the slightest touch? According to a growing corner of TikTok, the culprit could be your ferritin levels. Dubbed ‘ferritin face’, the viral new term links a collection of visible beauty changes to low ferritin, the protein responsible for storing iron in the body.

From ‘cortisol face’, the TikTok shorthand for facial puffiness allegedly linked to elevated stress, to the weight loss-adjacent ‘Ozempic face’, social media is now a hotbed for decoding what the body might be telling us in the mirror. So far, #FerritinFace has amassed more than 16 million views on TikTok, with videos of users attempting to identify the signs in their own appearance, offering advice on everything from supplements to traditional Chinese medicine, and even facial mapping. Since October, Google searches have been up 5,000% in the UK alone.
However, the conversation has also attracted a wave of caution from health professionals, warning against drawing medical conclusions from skin-deep assumptions.
points: Now, TikTok is diagnosing low iron through dark circles and thinning hair, cultivating the latest viral trend du jour.

articles.title: Nicole Kidman’s Fresh Fringe Is ‘Cool Without Trying’
articles.summary: Chanel’s first-ever show in Australia called for a special look, as per Nicole Kidman’s hairstylist Adir Abergel. He breaks down her new “Birkin” bangs.
body: Special occasions call for special beauty moments. At least, that was the case for Nicole Kidman, who showed off her new bangs for a historic moment: Chanel’s first-ever runway in Australia, where the Biarritz cruise collection was re-shown.

“Having Nicole back home in Sydney for [the show] felt really special,” hairstylist Adir Abergel tells Vogue exclusively. (While working closely with Kidman, the hairstylist can also be found crafting the punky crop of Kristen Stewart and Charlize Theron’s architectural micro bob.) Kidman was born in Honolulu, Hawaii, but moved to Sydney shortly after. “Matthieu’s collection is all about the seaside, and Sydney lives that: the harbor, the sandstone, the salt in the air. I wanted her hair to feel like part of that world. It’s easy, sun-kissed, a little undone, and cool without trying.”
points: Chanel’s first-ever show in Australia called for a special look, as per Nicole Kidman’s hairstylist Adir Abergel.

body: Lucky you: We’re sharing December’s BA Bake Club drop early so you can get started on holiday planning right…now!

This mousse has three foundational pastry techniques hidden in plain sight. It starts with a crème anglaise, a lusciously pourable custard. Adding that to a bowl of chopped chocolate yields a crémeux, a velvety and dense emulsified custard. Folding in whipped cream finally turns it into a fluffy mousse. Magical.
It’s important to use a 70% chocolate here. It’s intense enough to shine through the heavy cream and has enough cocoa butter to provide structure and stability, ensuring the mousse doesn’t slump.
A springform pan is a worthy and necessary investment, ensuring an anxiety-free presentation. It also allows you to bake and build the cake in just one tin.

body: As my plane touched down in Dallas, I could already make out my chauffeur waiting on the apron, the jet-black SUV glimmering in the Texas sun. It wasn’t long before my luggage was whisked away and we were driving across the airfield, past rows of planes waiting at their gates—so close that I could read their tail numbers. Our destination? A new private terminal operated by the company PS, which offers a curious promise to commercial fliers: Travel with us, and you will never step foot in the airport.
